fix/bestiary-globals — the classic-script -> ES-module globals bridge. data/bestiary.js, data/realm-bestiary.js, data/monster-flavor.js, and data/model-recipes.js each declare their payload as a top-level `const` (BESTIARY/REALM_BESTIARY/MONSTER_FLAVOR/MODEL_RECIPES). Classic <script> tags share one declarative scope, so other classic scripts see those consts as bare identifiers already (e.g. src/engine/theater-data.js reads PART_NAMES directly) — but top-level const/let, unlike var/function declarations, never attaches to `window`. An ES module (src/ui/ref-bestiary.js) has its own module scope and can only reach classic-script data through `window`, so before this fix window.BESTIARY etc. were always undefined and the Monster Manual's manualEntries() silently fell back to {} — empty grid, dead filters. This file runs after all four data consts (and after data/model-recipe-overrides.js) and republishes each one onto window explicitly (typeof-guarded, never redeclares them — owns nothing new, a pure republish) so any current or future ES-module Reference Shelf app has one shared, explicit seam instead of each module re-deriving its own defensive copy. Must load before any `<script type="module">` tag that reads these off window (today: src/ui/ref-bestiary.js). Added 2026-07-06 (fix/bestiary-globals).

The death→rebirth loop (docs/DEATH-AND-REBIRTH.md). Step 2: the bardo gap — rollBardoGap() is a 0–49 in-world-day bell roll (triangular, mode ~3–4 weeks); bardoGap(w,[days]) advances the world clock by the gap and turns the faction web once per elapsed week. Step 5: corpse + loot decay — a fallen PC's body+effects persist (set at death); corpseStatus(w,c) decays fresh→disturbed→gone by elapsed in-world days vs the body's CORPSE_CONTEXTS; corpsesAt(w,node) finds recoverable bodies; claimCorpse(w,c,taker) transfers the haul. DUNGEON-GRAPH.md U2 — semantics + scale domains, layered on U1's SpatialPlan. semanticizePlan(plan, segments, residents) extends a spatializePlan() output (never mutates it) with: (1) room roles from the corridor graph — entrance (entry segment) / finale (isFinale segment) / path (on the deterministic BFS critical path entry→finale) / pocket (degree-1 dead end, non-finale — HOOK-WALKS §4's parked branch-node idea's honest home) / side (everything else); (2) difficulty bands (room.band) from depth — shallow (depth 0-1, always)/mid/deep via a tertile split of [0,maxDepth], monotone non-decreasing along the critical path by construction (asserted, honest-fail on regression); (3) SCALE DOMAINS per law §2 ('a room that merely fits its monster is a prison') — every resident with scaleVsHuman>=2.0 claims its room + adjacent path/side rooms (patrol radius 1) at that scale; apex:true with scaleVsHuman>=4.0 claims the WHOLE dungeon instead; domain rooms get room.scaleDomain=max(current,scale), and any room below the fit-test minimum (ceil(scale)+2 cells per axis) is GROWN (re-carved, re-centered) with the plan's cells buffer fully rebuilt and BFS reachability re-verified from scratch (honest-fail if still unreachable); corridors inside a >1.0-scale domain get width>=2+heightScale; doors between differing-scale rooms get transition:true+squeeze:true (squeeze = geometry/DM hand-wave per Adam's ruling — no sprite/render work); (4) plan.domains[] ({scale,segNums,transitions:[doorIdx]}), always including the residual 1.0 human domain unless an apex claim consumed every room. Depends on SPATIAL_CELL (engine.place-spatialize's global) — must load after it. Pure engine-layer data code, no w/U/render/DOM, no RNG (fully deterministic function of its inputs). U3 (volumetric renderer)/U4 (walk binding) consume this output; rendering/walk-store writes/encounter-loot table wiring/beat content are out of scope here per spec.

THE BREACH & THE NIGHTMARE — engine layer (docs/BREACH.md, BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J2 'breach-core'/'outlandish-realms'). The walk-skin roll becomes a 2d10 bell + fray shift: rollWalkSkinBreach(envKind,{q,r,centerFn}) rolls breachShift2d10 (EXACT J2 rule: r>11 -> r+frayMod, r<11 -> r-frayMod, r==11 unchanged, clamp[2,20]; frayMod 0/+1/+2 off REGIONS-NAMES' own FRAY_1/FRAY_2), classifies the shifted result into center/nightmare/breach (NIGHTMARE_TAIL=3, BREACH_TAIL=19), and for center calls the caller's own bias-chain resolver (centerFn, defaulting to plain rollWalkSkin) BYTE-IDENTICAL to today; for a tail it rolls the compiled walk-breach-<env>/walk-nightmare-<env> table (breach-tables unit) and NULL-SAFE falls back to the center roll (tagged tailWanted) when that table isn't compiled yet — never crashes, never fabricates a row. breachPersistenceRoll(walk) — the d6 AT walk exit, once, idempotent (sealed 1-4/unstable 5/stable 6); breachStableDoor writes a write-once map-node flag for a stable outcome. breachMarkRealmActive/breachRealmWalkTaken/breachRealmClear own w.realm.debt (J2 mutation check: ONLY the original roll sets the 1d2 debt — a second call for an already-active realm is a pure no-op, never re-rolled/extended). The five physics-lens executors (breachPhysicsDcBump/ZoneStep/TechGate/HuntClock/StageVoice + the combatStart-adjacent breachApplyPhysicsToCombat wrapper) are PURE report-only functions — they compute the lens's delta and return a plain object; they never mutate HP/damage dice/AC/XP pricing and never patch any global (BREACH.md §2b's no-break invariant), leaving the actual fold-in to whichever call site (engine.check/engine.combat) chooses to read the reported delta. breachXpMultiplier(tail) is the single BREACH_XP/NIGHTMARE_XP (1.5, E(L) units) source for any future xpReport bucket. §6 (BREACH.md §2c/§2e.7, outlandish-realms unit): breachLootGuarantee(level,realms,segments) is THE ≥1-PER-BREACH GUARANTEE — rolls a flat-d4 channel (hoard/social/secret/apex), falls back social→hoard when the walk carries no Social segment (breachHasSocialSegment), then draws ONE realm-filtered Outlandish item via dwalkOutlandish(level,{inBreach:true,realms}) — inBreach:true is the ONE place reality-breaking is allowed outside the L4 gate's own level math (BREACH.md §2e.3's sourcing supersede, mirrored in src/engine/dungeon-walk.js's dwalkOutlandishAllowed). Every rollTable/frayBeyond1/frayBeyond2/mapOf/dwalkOutlandish read is typeof-guarded (BATCH-GUARDRAILS G9).

The Attitude/Parley/Morale RESOLVER (docs/SOCIAL.md §2-§4,§6; SOCIAL Phase 2) — the social analog of combat. PURE + DETERMINISTIC: every fn takes plain numbers/flags and returns a DELTA, never reading/writing the world. socialDC(value) = the DC to shift attitude one step friendlier (Hostile 25 → Friendly 10; Helpful terminal); applyLeverage(dc,levers) folds the NPC Want/Fear/Leverage/Trust-Lever mods (±5) and flags a decisive auto-shift; resolveSocialCheck(input) returns {outcome,from,to,shift,terrified,granted} (one check = one step; caught lie −2, miss-by-5 −1, intimidation overshoot → Terrified); moraleDC(trigger,mods)/resolveMorale(input) drive fight-or-flight (held vs. broke → caller rolls Morale Outcome); insightReadDC(input) = the scaled read-attitude DC (10 +5 guarded + best mental mod if masking). WIRING-SWEEP-A §3/§4 (docs/WIRING-MAP.md items 6-7, world.wiring-a): foe_morale now rolls parleyWantRoll on a "surrender" break (stashed foe.parleyWant) and huntedBehaviorRoll on a "flee"/"rout-panic" break (stashed foe.huntedBehavior); parley_open defaults p.want from a live combat foe's stashed parleyWant when the caller doesn't supply one. DM-SEAT (docs/DM-SEAT.md §5.1, feat/seat-app-module) — the API-direct DM transport: message assembly (§2), validation (§3), and the settings toggle (w.dm.transport==="seat"|"mailbox", default mailbox) that lets world.dm's sendTurn branch to this module WITHOUT changing the mailbox path. seatBoot() fetches docs/SEAT-PROMPT.md once per session with a clean degrade (missing file → seat disabled, toast, seatToggleTransport refuses to switch on). seatAssembleMessages builds the §2 four-part message array (system prompt / session-bootstrap once / rolling ~12-turn window with fold-to-summary eviction / this-turn digest) with BYTE-STABLE prefix ordering across calls (no timestamps/randomness woven in) for provider prompt-caching. seatEventVocabulary() reads the explicit DM_EVENT_TYPES registry (dm.js:1218) directly — no longer a source derivation (docs/SEAT-ADAPTER.md §2); the registry is parity-locked to applyEvent's switch by dev/verify-dm-seam.mjs's RED-FIRST guard — cached after first read. seatValidate() schema-gates a parsed TurnResponse and drops unknown-typed events with a dmNotes note; seatResolveResponse() retries ONCE on a parse failure with a corrective instruction, then falls back to seatStutterEnvelope() (an in-voice stall line — the session never crashes). seatSend() is sendTurn's seat-path counterpart: assembles+POSTs to the bridge's /seat route (built by a separate unit, feat/seat-bridge-proxy — this module never holds a provider key), streams SSE narration into the feed live via seatStreamAppend (render.js's renderDMFeed reads GS.seat.streamText while GS.seat.streaming), and — per §1 "events apply then, never mid-stream" — parses/validates/applies the TurnResponse only once the stream closes, reusing world.dm's real applyResponse (one implementation of the event-apply pipeline, seat or mailbox). Tested by dev/verify-seat.mjs (jsdom, mock /seat endpoint — no key needed).

Added 2026-07-02.

THE DURABILITY TRIO (docs/DURABILITY-TRIO.md) — three small batch-2 units bundled in one file/one verify harness (dev/verify-durability.mjs, per BATCH2-GUARDRAILS H1). §1 world export/import: exportUniverseJSON/exportWorldJSON serialize U (or one world wrapped in a minimal U) to pretty JSON; importUniverseJSON validates + merges BY WORLD ID, duplicating (never overwriting) a colliding id, running every incoming world through migrateWorld. Pure string-in/string-out — the DOM download/file-picker glue lives in genesis.html + the ⚙ Menu. §2 environmental rust: a non-magical METAL weapon/armor (rustIsMetalItem — data/items.js carries no material field, so this is a name/category heuristic reconciling the spec's trigger against what the generated data exposes, logged as an uncertainty) exposed to a qualifying hazard (rain-combat/submersion/acid — RUST_EXPOSURE_KINDS) rusts gently: first exposure sets `rusting` (a TELL, not in the generated ITEM_CONDITIONS vocab — written directly to inst.conditions rather than routed through the condition_add event's ITEM_CONDITIONS gate), a second un-maintained exposure upgrades to `rusted` (RUST_TEETH, already a parked ITEM_CONDITIONS entry per docs/ITEMS.md §D) — never worse. rustSteppedDie is the SRD weapon-die ladder step-down engine.combat's cmEquippedDamage consults for a rusted weapon; rustMaintainAll (called from passTime, any rest kind) clears every carried instance's rust. §3 Chronicle ⇐ Ledger: chronicleLine(entry) renders a ledger entry's existing `.text` as the Chronicle's HTML line (mostly passthrough + a per-type style class); chronicleMigrateLegacyLog(w) one-time-idempotently imports legacy w.log prose lines lacking a ledger twin as session-type ledger entries (stamped w._chronicleMigrated, called from migrateWorld); logEvent is redefined here as an INERT no-op shim (overriding world/state.js's w.log.unshift definition via classic-script late-declaration-wins) so its 16 existing call sites across world.play/creator.sheet/creator.levelup/world.fate/world.rebirth/engine.world-gen need no edits (every one already sits beside an equivalent addLedger call — G0 minimal-diffs). Added 2026-07-02 (durability unit, batch-2).

FOREVER STORAGE (docs/FOREVER-STORAGE.md, BATCH3-PLAN unit 13, BATCH3-GUARDRAILS J1/J2 "forever-guards") — the IndexedDB layer that keeps a many-session world off the localStorage wall. §1 saveWorld(w) persists ONLY the changed world, async, debounced (~250ms trailing, one timer per world id — saving world A never touches world B); world.state's saveU(u) is left untouched at all 37 call sites (G0 minimal-diffs) and ADDITIONALLY fires saveWorld for the active world off its synchronous localStorage write (the spec's own "keep the LS original for one release" belt-and-suspenders). migrateLStoIDB() is the boot-once import: every world in the legacy `genesis-universe-v2` blob writes into IDB, a read-back deep-equal verifies each one before the {migrated:true} stamp lands in the `meta` store — the LS blob is NEVER deleted this release, so a failed/partial migration always has the original to fall back to. storageEstimate() wraps navigator.storage.estimate() for the ⚙ Menu's storage meter (a dial, not a countdown — IDB is GB-scale). Every IDB write (storeWriteWorldNow/saveMeta/archiveAppend) is wrapped — a failure (including a real QuotaExceededError) surfaces storeHandleWriteFailure: an in-app toast + an immediate storeQuotaOffer export-download, never a silent loss; a plain no-idb ABSENCE (old browser / no shim) is explicitly NOT treated as a failure — it stays silent (saveU's synchronous localStorage write is the durable copy in that case). §2 archiveOldSessions(w) moves w.dmlog prose entries stamped with a session number <= (current session − HOT_SESSIONS, default 3) into the `archive` IDB store (one record per world id, append-only merge via archiveAppend) and strips them from the hot w.dmlog — the mechanical ledger (w.ledger) is NEVER touched here (it's small and IS the world's memory: recall/drift/reputation/chronicle all read it). archiveReadForWorld(worldId) is the Chronicle's on-demand read of what moved. The session stamp itself is a new additive field on pushDmLog's envelope (world.state — zero behavior change for existing dmlog readers, which ignore unknown keys). §3 game saves stay LOCKED ironman-always (docs/FOREVER-STORAGE.md §3) — nothing in this file adds a checkpoint/restore path; the retcon-negotiation protocol is DM-CHARTER frontier prose, explicitly out of this unit's code (BATCH-GUARDRAILS G0). storeMaybeBackupNudge() is the periodic "it's been 2 weeks — export a backup?" toast, tracked in the meta store (cosmetic scheduling, not durability-critical). NULL-SAFE throughout: no IndexedDB in the runtime (old browser, or a jsdom harness with no IDB shim) degrades every function here to a flagged {ok:false,reason:"no-idb"} — saveU's existing localStorage write is completely unaffected either way. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, forever-guards unit).

GAP-WIRING (docs/TABLE-GAPS-070126.md §7, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J2) — the wiring for five wave-2a tables that shipped fully compiled (100 rows each) with no caller: chase-complications, distant-word, downtime-ledger, festival-and-holy-days, shrine-and-omen. §1 chase: chaseInit/chaseRound/chaseYield are a PURE 3-segment gap-clock (mirrors engine.combat/engine.social — operate only on the passed transient chase object; the caller owns GS.chase + ledger commits), closing on a caller-supplied pursuerWon boolean from an already-resolved opposed check, rolling one chase-complications result per round, ending in outcome:"contact"|"away". §2 distant-word: distantWordFactPool/distantWordPick salience-weight (recency-doubled, most-recent-30-days) over clock|outcome|drift ledger entries from NON-current nodes; distantWordRoll binds a Distortion row to a REAL picked fact (never invents one — degrades to fact:null rather than fabricate, the spec's named mutation check) and leaves a Color row fact-free by design; `dm.realFact` carries the true text for the DM's eyes only. §3 downtime: fixed DOWNTIME_INTENTS vocab (work/carouse/research/train/lie-low/seek-work); seek-work flags {ok:false,reason:"seek-work-unbuilt"} (routes to JOB-WALKS, not yet built — never faked, G9); the other five roll downtime-ledger once, parse payout hooks via downtimePayoutFromText (gold sign/qualifier, contact-mint/distant-word/condition/thread flags) and tier-scale gold via downtimeGoldAmount (DOWNTIME_BASE_BY_TIER, mirrors ECONOMY-SINKS' LODGING_GP tier curve). §4 festival: festivalEligibleFromDrift reports whether a drift band is Textured+ (chain-eligible, caller/DM decides); festivalRoll surfaces the roll + its own marketEffect/complication text (applying a live price multiplier is ECONOMY/SHOP-UI's job, out of scope). §5 shrine & omen: shrineOmenRoll binds every row's `` `[the myth]` `` placeholder to the world's own w.seed.myth (never invents a myth; a myth-less world leaves the placeholder, flagged not fabricated). NULL-SAFE throughout: every rollTable() call degrades to a logged no-op if a table isn't compiled (matches WORLD-TURN's convention), though all five ARE compiled today. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, gap-wiring unit).

URBAN FABRIC (docs/URBAN-FABRIC.md, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J2 "urban-fabric") — typed buildings, lazy districts, the tavern as a surface. §1 rollBuilding(type,opts): the building-interior base roll + a data.building-kits TYPE KIT; shop kinds (smithy/apothecary/general/arcanist) delegate to makeShop wholesale (the kit adds the room around the counter, economy.js stays the sole stock owner); the tavern kit's namePattern ("tavern-name") consumes the Tavern-2.0-extraction compiled table. §2 district fabric (Settlement 1.1, distilled): mintDistricts(w,nodeId) mints write-once `kind:"district"` codex records linked `part-of` the node, ONCE per node (a re-entry no-ops, returning the existing ids — the J1 mutation check); districtCount(tier) is the PLACE_TIERS-keyed count (hamlet 0 · village 1 · town 1d2 · city 1d3+1); each district rolls `urban-district-type` for its character line. §3 building lifecycle: buildingApproach mints a typed building SOFT at a node — its proprietor draws from the ambient-pool path first (an already-minted soft ambient NPC at the node, per J2's "proprietors mint via the ambient-pool path"), rolling a fresh rollNPC only if none is free; buildingContact locks the building AND its proprietor to hard canon together (codexContact on both), mirroring how every other entity's soft->hard lock works. §4 the tavern's system-surfaces: tavernContactFire re-fires gap-wiring's distantWordRoll on tavern contact (no new mechanism); carouse already routes through gap-wiring's generic downtimeIntent (a tavern is simply WHERE that intent gets declared, not a second venue gate); the proprietor being minted `at` the node satisfies prep.js's nodeOwnerAttitude for free (the lodging-owner tint). WIRING-SWEEP-A §6 (docs/WIRING-MAP.md item 5, world.wiring-a): buildingContact's tavern branch also rolls tavernEncounterRoll — a chance-gated (0.35) tavern-encounters ambient beat. NULL-SAFE throughout (matches WORLD-TURN's convention): an unknown type, missing kit data, or an uncompiled table all degrade to a flagged {ok:false,reason} or a null sub-field, never a fabricated result. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, urban-fabric unit).

JOB WALKS (docs/JOB-WALKS.md, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J1/J2 "job-walks") — the 300-row npc-job-board SCALES (pay + threat by place tier) and accepting a posting MINTS a real 1-3 segment walk (Adam's directive: "infinite quests!"). §1 jobPosting/jobBoardRead: one/2-3 tier-scaled postings per board read — tier from nodeLodgingTier + region econTilt (the same signals ECONOMY-SINKS/open_shop already reuse, no new heuristic), pay = TIER_PAY[tier] mildly tier-compounded, envHint a uniform urban/wilderness/dungeon roll (the row text carries no env tag — a guessed text-match would violate G9, so this is a fresh roll), poster a rolled NPC minted soft into the codex. §2 jobWalkAccept: segments = 1+tier via jobWalkSegCount, threat=tier, routed to rollUrbanWalk (urban, stays at the current node) or rollWildernessWalk/rollDungeonWalk (wilderness/dungeon — OFF-city per §3, mints a fresh destination node + rolls a route exactly like play.js's explore()); stores under prep.js's P.nodes keyed by the (possibly-new) destination node with kind:"job", activates via walkSetActive — a REAL walk with real provenance, nothing bespoke. jobWalkPayout (called from prep.js's walkComplete kind:"job" branch): pays gold directly onto the living sheet, warms the poster's attitude + locks them to a real contact on completion (recurring employers), flags followUp. §3 jobBoardTick (wired into worldTurn's montage branch, src/world/turn.js): the TTL sweep (4+1d4 days) that resolves an unclaimed posting WITHOUT the player — 1d6: 1-3 someone-else-took-it (ledger line only), 4-6 it-got-worse (bumps the poster's linked faction clock +1 IF repuFactionOf resolves one; a bare rolled NPC carries no faction link in this codebase today, so that half degrades to a flagged no-op rather than inventing an attribution — this is the mutation check the spec names: "persist forever" fails once this sweep exists and is called). gap-wiring.js's downtimeIntent seek-work branch now calls jobBoardRead directly (closing that unit's flagged no-op). NULL-SAFE throughout: an uncompiled npc-job-board, a missing walk roller, or an unknown posting id all degrade to a flagged {ok:false,reason}, never a fabricated result. Added 2026-07-02 (batch-3, job-walks unit).

WIRING-SWEEP-A (docs/WIRING-MAP.md §B Wave A, docs/BATCH3-PLAN.md unit 10, docs/BATCH3-GUARDRAILS.md J1 "wiring-sweep-A") — the Wave-A wire-in queue minus npc-job-board (promoted to its own unit, job-walks.js): the remaining seven true orphans. §1 REST-RISK: restRiskRoll grades a rest's SECURITY CLASS (inn/camp/wild/dungeon, derived from nodeLodgingTier+nodeInhabited+the walk env — the only real per-node signals this codebase carries) and rolls the matching urban-/dungeon-rest-complications table; a row whose OWN TEXT reads as a violent interruption can INTERRUPT the rest (restRiskSevere — never a guessed Spice band, neither table carries one). Wired into play.js's passTime. §2 IF-IGNORED: turnIgnoredCheck sweeps codex thread records (dm.legs hook/thread-seed, unresolved) stale past IGNORED_STALE_DAYS, rolls npc-if-ignored (+regional-effects when region-tagged), ledgers a drift entry, and resets the staleness window — wired into worldTurn's montage branch (src/world/turn.js), same shape as repuFadeTick/jobBoardTick. §3 parleyWantRoll: creature-parley-wants rolled by monster-tactics' morale seam (src/world/dm.js foe_morale) the instant a foe breaks to "surrender" — stashed as foe.parleyWant, SOCIAL's parley_open defaults p.want from it when the caller doesn't supply one. §4 huntedBehaviorRoll: monster-behavior-if-hunted rolled the instant a foe breaks to "flee"/"rout-panic" — stashed as foe.huntedBehavior (feeds a future chase_start caller; that caller is gap-wiring's own flagged-open follow-up, out of this unit's scope — see file header). §5 regionEncounterRoll: region-encounter as an additive per-leg regional-flavor roll, gated on a region actually being present (null region ⇒ null, byte-identical fallback). The "malformed header" flag did NOT reproduce against current source/compiled reality (hand-verified before writing this file, G9) — no repair needed. §6 tavernEncounterRoll: tavern-encounters as a chance-gated (0.35) ambient beat alongside urban.js's buildingContact tavern branch. §7 walkPickInteractable: urban-interactable-object/wilderness-interactable-object — the same segment-object slot dungeon-walk.js already wires for dungeons, called from src/engine/walk.js (urban) and src/engine/wild-walk.js (wilderness) per non-finale segment/leg. §8 seed dispatch (urban-rumor-intel/urban-catalyst + the ≥1-non-urban-seed rider): VERIFIED already wired (rollUrbanWalk's existing Rumor branch + setup.catalyst/finale catalystCallback) and already structurally guaranteed (engine.prep-bundle's pbundlePlan always assembles one each of urban/dungeon/wilderness) — no code change needed, harness verifies the property directly.
